newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strikes go with democracy, says SAfrica's Mboweni.
newsitem.headline: Strikes go with democracy, says SAfrica's Mboweni.

text.p: South African Labour Minister Tito Mboweni on Thursday defended Cosatu's right to strike, saying it was part of the democratic process.
Asked his view of a threat by the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) to stage fresh strikes in protest at planned labour legislation, Mboweni told a news conference:
"It's in the nature of negotiations for parties to use whatever power is in within their disposal to ensure their point of view is heard."
He said labour action was one of the consequences of the "open, democratic society for which we have striven so long".
"We must be careful that whatever we do, we don't undermine that...As long as procedures are followed, and the issues are relevant, that's part and parcel of democracy."
Mboweni was speaking before going into a meeting with Business South Africa on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
"They have not indicated in their request for an urgent meeting what the exact detail of the issue will be...
"Depending on the nature of the meeting, and the cordiality or otherwise of that meeting, we are hoping to have a very short press briefing," Mboweni said.
